prompt: For 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = −197 kJ. Which change increases the value of K?
markscheme: **B.** Only temperature changes K; lowering T favours the exothermic forward reaction.

prompt: At equilibrium in a 1.0 dm³ flask there are 0.20 mol H₂, 0.20 mol I₂ and 1.6 mol HI. What is K for H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI?

2.00 mol of NO₂ is placed in a sealed 1.00 dm³ container and allowed to reach equilibrium: 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g). At equilibrium 0.60 mol of N₂O₄ is present.

**(a)** Calculate K. **[3]**

**(b)** A further 0.50 mol of N₂O₄ is added. Calculate Q and predict the direction of the change. **[2]**

**(c)** State the effect of this addition on the value of K. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** [NO₂] at equilibrium $= 2.00 - 2(0.60) = 0.80$ ✓; $K = \tfrac{0.60}{0.80^2}$ ✓ $= 0.94$ ✓

**(b)** $Q = \tfrac{1.10}{0.80^2} = 1.7$ ✓; Q > K so the reaction shifts backwards (towards NO₂) ✓

**(c)** No change (temperature constant) ✓
